relevant_findings.topic: EA-based unit of measure despite large surface area per door
relevant_findings.finding: Garage doors are counted as EA (each) via PS_EXT_OPENING_EA.DOOR_GARAGE. Each garage door is 1 EA regardless of size. However, garage doors are LARGE surfaces: single doors (8x7, 9x7 ft = 56-63 SF), double doors (16x7, 18x7 ft = 112-126 SF). Despite the large SF, the EA unit is appropriate because the door is a single discrete assembly painted as one unit. The internal production rates (spray SF/hr) convert EA to time using the door's known SF. Door size (single vs double) is a modifier within EA, not a separate counting unit.

relevant_findings.topic: Three substrate types with distinct coating requirements
relevant_findings.finding: Garage doors come in three substrate types: (1) Sectional steel — industry standard for modern NC (~85% of installations). Factory-applied polyester or fluorocarbon (Kynar) finish with residual wax layer from fabrication/transit. Susceptible to rust if substrate exposed. (2) Wood panel — premium, highly hygroscopic, requires tannin management for cedar/redwood species. DASMA TDS #162 mandates six-side sealing. (3) Carriage-style — high-complexity architectural doors with decorative overlays, crossbucks, window lites. Often mix materials (steel base + wood/composite overlays). High risk of differential expansion.

relevant_findings.topic: Factory wax removal is critical unique prep step for steel doors
relevant_findings.finding: Steel sectional garage doors arrive with a residual wax layer from fabrication and transit protection. This wax is the primary obstacle to adhesion. Protocol: scuff with gray 3M synthetic steel wool pad (#000 equivalent) saturated with biodegradable cleaning solution. Without wax removal, new acrylic over factory finish results in catastrophic peeling — the #1 failure mode for garage door painting.

relevant_findings.topic: Deglossing required after wax removal on steel doors
relevant_findings.finding: Factory fluorocarbon/silicone-polyester finishes require mechanical tooth for adhesion after wax removal. Methods: (1) Mechanical — 120-150 grit sandpaper. (2) Chemical — liquid deglosser. Adhesion must be verified with ASTM D3359 tape test before primer application. If adhesion test fails, escalate to more aggressive removal or Brush-Off Blast Cleaning (SSPC-SP7).

relevant_findings.topic: DTM primer required for steel garage doors
relevant_findings.finding: Direct-to-Metal (DTM) primers are formulated with rust-inhibitive pigments and high volume solids (~46%). They provide flash-rust resistance (prevents oxidation while waterborne coating is wet) and remain flexible enough for thermal expansion of steel panels. DTM primer is mandatory for all steel garage doors after wax removal and deglossing. For bare metal (rare in NC), zinc-rich epoxy primer is required after SSPC cleaning.

relevant_findings.topic: Leapfrog painting technique for articulation joints
relevant_findings.finding: Sectional garage doors have hinged joints between panels. Paint bridging across these joints is a critical failure mode — opening the door rips paint off or damages the opener motor. The 'leapfrog' technique prevents this: paint panels alternately (e.g., panels 1,3,5 then 2,4,6). Each joint is opened, painted, and dried tack-free before moving to the next section. The door must be manually articulated during painting.

The bottom weatherseal (astragal) is highly compressible and bonds easily to wet paint and driveway thresholds. Methods to prevent adhesion: (1) Mechanical spacing — prop door 2-4 inches above threshold during full 24-48 hour cure. (2) Seal removal — remove seal and retainer entirely for clean six-side finish access, reinstall after cure. (3) Threshold protection — wax paper or paraffin wax on driveway as emergency release. Bottom seal avoidance is a mandatory task for every garage door painting project.

Four complexity levels: (1) Standard flush panel — 1.00x baseline, continuous roller/spray. (2) Raised/recessed panel — 1.10x, manual brush work in recesses. (3) Carriage-style overlay — 1.25-1.40x, meticulous masking, multi-tone cutting of decorative elements. (4) Integrated windows — +0.5-1.5 hours per door, masking individual divided lites. Panel complexity and windows are independent modifiers that stack.

relevant_findings.topic: Spray is the primary application method for garage door faces
relevant_findings.finding: Large flat panels are ideal for airless spray application. Production rates: spray 150-300 SF/hr, roller 100-150 SF/hr, brush 50-75 SF/hr. Per Application Methods Doctrine, metal doors should be spray-only — back-rolling AVOIDED on metal doors (introduces orange peel). Spray tip for metal doors: 0.010-0.014 inch orifice (310, 412 tip codes). Brush is used only for panel recesses on raised-panel doors and detail work on carriage-style doors. Roller is acceptable as a secondary method for wood panel doors.
relevant_findings.source: Exterior_Garage_Doors_Doctrine.md §5; Exterior_Application_Methods_Doctrine.md Part A §1, Part B §6

relevant_findings.topic: LRV restriction for carriage and composite doors
relevant_findings.finding: Carriage-style, composite, or vinyl garage doors must have LRV > 55. Dark colors (LRV < 55) absorb excessive solar energy causing warping, shrinkage, and voided warranties. Steel doors are more tolerant (LRV > 30 recommended, IR-reflective coatings recommended below 30). This is a HARD STOP for carriage/composite doors — LRV < 55 is not permitted without IR-reflective technology.

relevant_findings.topic: Six-side sealing for wood garage doors (DASMA TDS #162)
relevant_findings.finding: DASMA Technical Data Sheet #162 governs finishing of wood garage doors. All six sides must be primed and finished. Failure to seal hidden edges (back face, top/bottom edges, side edges) is the primary cause of rot and warranty voidance. Wood garage doors are highly hygroscopic — they constantly exchange moisture with the environment. Tannin management required for cedar/redwood species (alkyd stain-blocking primer).

relevant_findings.topic: Spring tension and balance test checkpoint
relevant_findings.finding: Garage doors use high-tension counterbalance systems (torsion or extension springs). Paint adds weight which can unbalance the door. A properly balanced door lifts with less than 10 lbs of force. Heavy coatings on an out-of-balance door can destroy the opener or snap springs. A balance test checkpoint is recommended after painting — not an estimation line item but an SOP quality gate.

Three categories of exclusion zones that must NOT be painted: (1) Weatherstripping contact surfaces — paint destroys seal flexibility. (2) Spring mechanism hardware — torsion springs, cables, brackets. (3) Track and roller contact points — paint causes binding. These zones require masking protection before spray application.

relevant_findings.topic: Topcoat is 100% exterior acrylic latex for all substrates
relevant_findings.finding: Standard topcoat for all garage door substrates (steel, wood, carriage) is 100% exterior acrylic latex. Provides superior flexibility for thermal expansion, UV screening, and breathability. Applied in 2 coats for NC. The same chemistry works across all three substrates — the primer is what varies by substrate.

Valid sheens for garage doors: satin, semi-gloss, gloss. Per Color/Sheen Doctrine, doors receive satin, semi-gloss, or gloss — project-level selection with no locked-in default. Higher sheen adds durability on this weather-exposed surface. Semi-gloss is the most common choice for garage doors due to balance of durability and forgiving finish quality.

relevant_findings.topic: Masking-to-spray labor ratio for garage doors
relevant_findings.finding: Standard masking-to-spray ratio is 3:1 to 4:1 (masking hours to spray hours) for exterior spray projects. For garage doors specifically, masking requirements include: driveway/apron protection, adjacent siding masking, window glass masking (if integrated), weatherstrip masking, track and hardware masking. Spray on a single garage door requires significant masking setup relative to the spray time due to the concentrated overspray zone at driveway level.

relevant_findings.topic: Driveway and apron protection is critical
relevant_findings.finding: Garage doors sit directly above driveways. Driveway protection is mandatory during spray operations. Broom-finish concrete is high porosity (hard to clean). Decorative pavers have joints that absorb paint. Protection methods: absorbent runners with 6-mil poly for concrete, reinforced poly sheeting with taped edges for pavers. Canvas drop cloths for asphalt (breathable, non-slip). Standard plastic sheeting is a SAFETY HAZARD on hardscapes — becomes slippery when wet with paint.

relevant_findings.topic: Window masking for garage doors with integrated windows
relevant_findings.finding: Many garage doors include small window inserts (typically in the top panel). These require individual masking with HDPE static-cling film. Carriage-style doors may have divided-lite window patterns requiring extensive masking. Window masking adds 0.5-1.5 hours per door depending on lite count and pattern. This is an additive modifier on top of the panel complexity multiplier.

condition_drivers.impact: Drives primer selection, surface prep protocol, and failure mode profile. Steel = wax removal + degloss + DTM primer. Wood = sand + six-side sealing (DASMA TDS #162) + alkyd stain-blocker for tannin species. Carriage = mixed-material prep (steel base + wood/composite overlays) + decorative element masking + LRV > 55 restriction.
condition_drivers.notes: This is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION — changes task structure, not just rate. Steel is ~85% of NC garage doors.

condition_drivers.impact: Determines prep depth and primer requirement. Factory-primed (steel) = wax removal + degloss + DTM primer (factory primer alone is NOT adequate — wax layer must be removed). Bare wood = full sand + prime + six-side seal. Bare metal = SSPC cleaning + zinc-rich primer. Note: unlike entry doors, factory-primed steel garage doors STILL need wax removal and DTM primer over factory finish.
condition_drivers.notes: SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY is dominant NC state for steel doors. SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD is dominant for wood panel doors.

condition_drivers.impact: Production rate multiplier: flush = 1.00x baseline, raised_panel = 1.10x (brush work in recesses), carriage = 1.25-1.40x (overlay masking, multi-tone cutting), windows = +0.5-1.5 hrs additive. Panel_complexity and windows are INDEPENDENT modifiers that stack.
condition_drivers.notes: This is a MODIFIER DIMENSION — changes rate but not task structure (except windows adds masking tasks).

condition_drivers.impact: QT3: standard 2-coat with clean edges and leapfrog technique. QT4: premium materials, light sand between finish coats, raking light inspection for runs/sags/holidays. QT2 excluded (visible from street). QT5 excluded (utility surface, not fine finish).
condition_drivers.notes: Narrow 2-tier range reflects the utility character of garage doors — they need good protection and appearance but are not architectural showcase elements.

condition_drivers.impact: Project-level selection with no locked-in default. Higher sheen adds weather durability. Gloss requires higher prep quality. Semi-gloss is the most common for garage doors.

Single doors (8x7, 9x7 ft = 56-63 SF). Double doors (16x7, 18x7 ft = 112-126 SF). Door size is a rate modifier — double doors take approximately 1.8-2.0x the time of a single door (not exactly 2x because setup/cleanup is fixed). Size affects material quantity directly.
condition_drivers.notes: This is a MODIFIER DIMENSION. The PS key counts doors as EA regardless of size.

quality_differences.description: Standard garage door. Steel: wax removal + degloss + DTM primer + 2 finish coats with mid-grade 100% acrylic exterior latex. Leapfrog technique for joints. Bottom seal avoidance. Wood: sand + prime + six-side seal + 2 finish coats. Clean edges at windows, hardware, and adjacent surfaces.
quality_differences.typical_use: Standard NC residential garage doors. Most common tier.

quality_differences.description: Premium garage door. Same as QT3 plus: premium materials (SW Emerald, BM Aura). Light sand between finish coats (220-grit). Raking light inspection for runs, sags, holidays. Extra care on carriage-style decorative elements. Crisp masking lines at windows.
quality_differences.typical_use: Upscale residential, architect-specified carriage-style doors, wood panel doors on custom homes.

failure_modes.name: Catastrophic peeling from residual factory wax
failure_modes.description: New acrylic paint applied over residual factory wax or Kynar finish without proper wax removal and bonding primer. The entire paint film peels in sheets, often within weeks of application.
failure_modes.prevention: Mandatory wax removal protocol: gray 3M synthetic steel wool pad + biodegradable cleaner. Followed by deglossing (120-150 grit). ASTM D3359 adhesion verification. DTM primer before topcoat.
failure_modes.detection: Paint peeling in large sheets. Paint easily lifts with fingernail. Poor cross-hatch adhesion test.

failure_modes.name: Articulation joint paint bridging — door glued shut
failure_modes.description: Painting the door in the closed position causes paint to bridge across the articulation joints between panels. Opening the door rips the paint film at every joint, leaving ragged edges. Repeated bridging can bind the door, stalling or damaging the opener motor.
failure_modes.prevention: Mandatory leapfrog technique: paint alternating panels (1,3,5 then 2,4,6), opening each joint to dry tack-free before painting adjacent panels. Never paint in fully closed position.
failure_modes.detection: Paint tearing at panel joints when door operates. Ragged paint lines at hinges. Opener motor straining.

failure_modes.name: Thermal deformation from dark colors on carriage/composite doors
failure_modes.description: Dark colors (LRV < 55) absorb excessive solar energy on carriage-style and composite garage doors. Causes warping, shrinkage, overlay delamination, and voided manufacturer warranties.
failure_modes.prevention: HARD STOP: LRV must be > 55 for carriage/composite doors. Steel doors are more tolerant (LRV > 30, with IR-reflective recommended below 30). If homeowner insists on dark color for carriage door, require written warranty waiver and IR-reflective coating.
failure_modes.detection: Door panel warping. Overlay separation. Panel gaps widening in sun exposure.

failure_modes.name: Bottom seal adhesion to driveway
failure_modes.description: Bottom weatherseal (astragal) bonds to wet paint on its compression surface against the driveway threshold. Door reopening tears the seal, damages the paint, and may pull driveway coating.
failure_modes.prevention: Prop door 2-4 inches above threshold during full 24-48 hour cure. Alternatively, remove bottom seal and retainer before painting, reinstall after cure. Emergency: wax paper on driveway threshold as release agent.
failure_modes.detection: Seal stuck to driveway when opening. Torn weatherseal. Paint pulled from bottom panel edge.

failure_modes.name: Tannin bleed on wood doors
failure_modes.description: Cedar and redwood species release tannin extractives that bleed through acrylic primers, causing brown/yellow staining of the finish coat.
failure_modes.prevention: Apply alkyd stain-blocking primer on tannin-rich species. Acrylic primers may require two coats to block severe tannin staining. Spot-prime visible knots with alkyd primer before full surface acrylic primer.
failure_modes.detection: Brown or yellowish staining bleeding through white or light-colored finish coats, especially on sun-exposed panels.

failure_modes.name: Wood rot from incomplete six-side sealing
failure_modes.description: Failure to seal all six sides of wood garage door panels per DASMA TDS #162 allows moisture wicking through unsealed end-grain and back surfaces. Leads to rot, panel distortion, and warranty voidance.
failure_modes.prevention: Mandatory six-side sealing per DASMA TDS #162. All edges (including top, bottom, and back face) must be primed and finished. Back face access may require door disassembly or painting before installation.
failure_modes.detection: Panel swelling. End-grain darkening. Paint cracking at panel joints. Soft wood at bottom edges.

primer_systems.name: Acrylic DTM (Direct-to-Metal) Primer
primer_systems.description: Rust-inhibitive DTM primer for steel garage doors. High volume solids (~46%), flash-rust resistance, flexible for thermal expansion. Applied after wax removal and deglossing.
primer_systems.notes: Required for ALL steel garage doors in NC — factory primer alone is NOT adequate due to wax contamination. Provides adhesion bridge between deglossed factory finish and topcoat.

primer_systems.name: 100% Acrylic Latex Exterior Primer
primer_systems.description: Standard exterior primer for bare wood garage doors. Remains flexible, breathable, good tannin blocking for most wood species.
primer_systems.notes: Primary primer for bare wood garage doors. For tannin-rich species (cedar/redwood), supplement with alkyd spot-prime at knots or use two coats.

primer_systems.name: Alkyd Stain-Blocking Primer
primer_systems.description: Alkyd primer for superior tannin stain blocking on cedar, redwood, and Douglas fir garage door panels. Deep penetration into wood substrate.
primer_systems.recoat_time: 2-4 hours (may extend to 3-5 days for full cure on tannin-rich wood)
primer_systems.notes: Required when wood species is cedar, redwood, or fir. NOT for galvanized metal. May be used as full-surface primer or as spot-prime for knots under acrylic primer.

primer_systems.name: Bonding Primer
primer_systems.description: Bonding primer for composite overlay panels on carriage-style doors. Grips slick composite surfaces while providing tooth for topcoat. Required when carriage overlays are factory-finished or have glossy composite surfaces.
primer_systems.recoat_time: Within 1 week (loses flexibility if left exposed too long)
primer_systems.notes: Conditional — only needed when carriage overlays have glossy/sealed composite surfaces that reject standard primers.

topcoat_systems.name: 100% Acrylic Latex Exterior Paint
topcoat_systems.description: Standard exterior acrylic latex finish for garage doors. Superior UV resistance, flexibility for thermal expansion, excellent adhesion. Mid-grade products.
topcoat_systems.notes: QT3 mid-grade: SW SuperPaint, BM Regal Select, or equivalent. Works on all three substrates (steel, wood, carriage).

topcoat_systems.name: Premium 100% Acrylic Latex Exterior Paint
topcoat_systems.description: Premium exterior acrylic latex finish for garage doors. Maximum UV resistance, self-cleaning technology, superior color retention.
topcoat_systems.notes: QT4 premium: SW Emerald, BM Aura, or equivalent. Used for upscale carriage-style and wood panel doors.

notes_for_materials_manager: All garage door substrates use 100% acrylic latex exterior topcoat — same chemistry across steel, wood, and carriage.
Steel doors: DTM primer is MANDATORY after wax removal/degloss. Factory primer alone is NOT adequate (unlike exterior entry doors where factory primer is acceptable base).
Wood doors: 100% acrylic exterior primer. Alkyd stain-blocker for tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood, fir).
Carriage composite overlays may need bonding primer if overlay surfaces are glossy/sealed.
LRV restriction: carriage/composite doors LRV > 55. Steel doors LRV > 30 (IR-reflective recommended below 30).
Coverage rate for garage door surfaces: 300-400 SF/gal per coat. Single door = 56-63 SF, double door = 112-126 SF.
Spray tip for metal doors: 310 or 412 (0.010-0.014 inch orifice). 100-mesh blue filter for enamel on steel.
3M gray synthetic steel wool pads needed for wax removal — these are a prep consumable, not applicator.
Biodegradable cleaner/degreaser for wax removal protocol.
Window masking materials: HDPE static-cling film for garage door window inserts.
Driveway protection materials: canvas drop cloths (non-slip) or absorbent floor mats. Standard poly sheeting is a safety hazard on hardscapes.
notes_for_sop_librarian: Module structure: setup (protection) -> prep (wax removal / degloss / sand) -> prime -> apply_coat_1 -> interstage (QT4 sand between) -> apply_coat_2 -> cleanup (bottom seal management, teardown).

CRITICAL: Leapfrog painting technique is MANDATORY for all sectional garage doors. Paint alternating panels (1,3,5 then 2,4,6). Each joint must be opened and dried tack-free before painting adjacent panel. This is an SOP process note, not a separate task — it modifies the apply task execution.
Bottom seal management: prop door 2-4 inches above threshold during 24-48 hour cure. Or remove seal/retainer before painting, reinstall after cure. This IS a separate task.
Wax removal (steel only): gray 3M pad + cleaner. Separate task from deglossing.
Deglossing (steel only): 120-150 grit after wax removal. Separate from wax removal.
ASTM D3359 adhesion test (steel only): tape test after degloss, before primer. If fails, escalate to SSPC-SP7. This is a QA checkpoint.
Six-side sealing (wood only): per DASMA TDS #162. All six sides must be primed and finished. Back face access may require painting before installation.
Balance test checkpoint: recommended after painting. Weight of paint can affect spring balance. SOP quality gate, not billable task.
Exclusion zone masking: weatherstrip contact surfaces, spring mechanism hardware, track and roller contact points. Mask before spray application.
Window masking: top-panel window inserts. HDPE static-cling film. Divided-lite carriage windows require individual pane masking.
Driveway/apron protection: mandatory for spray application. Canvas drops or absorbent mats.
Adjacent siding masking: mask siding around garage door opening when spraying.
notes_for_estimation_engineer: This is an EA-BASED spec. Production rates are hours/EA, NOT SF/hr.
Door size modifier: single door (56-63 SF) = 1.00x baseline, double door (112-126 SF) = 1.80-2.00x.
Panel complexity modifiers: flush = 1.00x, raised_panel = 1.10x, carriage = 1.25-1.40x, windows = +0.5-1.5 hrs additive.
Base production rate (spray, single flush steel door, QT3): estimated 2.0-3.0 hrs/EA total (all phases: setup, prep, prime, 2 coats, cleanup, bottom seal management).
Base production rate (spray, double flush steel door, QT3): estimated 3.5-5.5 hrs/EA total.
Wood door adds: six-side sealing overhead (+0.5-1.0 hrs/EA for back face and edge access).
Wax removal + degloss (steel): 0.50-1.0 hrs/EA for single, 0.75-1.5 hrs/EA for double. Included in base rate.
Driveway/apron protection: 0.25-0.50 hrs/EA (setup + teardown). Scales with driveway SF if PS key is available.
Adjacent siding masking: 0.25-0.50 hrs/EA for spray method.
Substrate material modifier: steel = 1.00 (baseline), wood = 1.15 (six-side seal + grain management), carriage = 1.25 (mixed materials + overlay detail).
QT modifier: QT3 = 1.00, QT4 = 1.15 (sand between coats + premium materials + inspection).
Environmental conditions EXCLUDED from estimation — SOP concerns only (per sibling spec pattern).
Coat system: DTM primer + 2 finish coats for steel. Acrylic primer + 2 finish coats for wood. Factory-primed steel STILL gets DTM primer (wax removal makes factory primer inadequate alone).
Material consumption: spray at 50-70% transfer efficiency. Budget 25-33% more material than brush/roll baseline.
Access is typically ground-level. No height modifier for standard garage doors.
Grand entry rate for exterior doors should NOT overlap — garage doors are separate from entry doors.

assumptions.value: New construction garage doors only — sectional steel, wood panel, carriage-style. Exterior face only (interior/garage-side face is NOT in scope for exterior painting spec). Does not include: entry doors (SF_DOOR_EXT_NC_v1), garage door trim/casing (SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1), garage interior walls.
assumptions.note: Garage door exterior face only. Interior (garage-side) face may be a future spec or handled as interior scope.

assumptions.value: QT3-QT4 only. QT2 excluded (visible from street — not economy-appropriate). QT5 excluded (utility surface, not architectural showcase like entry doors).
assumptions.note: Narrow 2-tier range is appropriate for garage doors. Entry doors (SF_DOOR_EXT_NC_v1) support QT3-QT5 because they are focal architectural elements.

assumptions.value: Repaint substrate states excluded from this NC spec.
assumptions.note: Repaint adds significant labor for existing coating removal, adhesion testing, and feathering. Requires separate spec.

assumptions.value: Factory-primed steel garage doors STILL require DTM primer over the factory finish after wax removal and deglossing.
assumptions.note: This is DIFFERENT from exterior entry doors where factory primer is acceptable as topcoat base. Garage door factory finish has wax contamination that makes the factory primer layer unreliable even after cleaning. DTM primer provides a fresh adhesion bridge.

assumptions.value: Spray is the primary application method. Roller is secondary for wood only. Brush is detail-only.
assumptions.note: Back-rolling is AVOIDED on metal doors per Application Methods Doctrine.

assumptions.value: Only the street-facing exterior face of the garage door is in scope. The garage-interior face is not scoped under this exterior spec.
assumptions.source: Standard practice — garage interior face is either left unpainted or handled as interior scope
assumptions.note: Doctrine does not explicitly address interior face scope for garage doors. Standard NC practice paints exterior face only. DASMA TDS #162 six-side sealing for wood doors would include back face as part of sealing obligation — clarify with Eric whether back face painting is included in six-side seal or is full finish.

uncertainties.topic: Back face of wood garage doors — six-side seal vs full finish
uncertainties.detail: DASMA TDS #162 requires six-side sealing for wood garage doors. The back face (garage-interior side) must be at minimum primed and sealed. Whether it receives full finish coats (2 coats like the front) or just primer/sealer is unclear from doctrine. Full finish on back face doubles the application area and adds significant time.
uncertainties.recommendation: Assume six-side sealing means primer + 1 coat on back face (sealing obligation) — not full 2-coat finish. This is the minimum to satisfy DASMA TDS #162. If full finish on back face is needed, it should be scoped as an add-on modifier.

uncertainties.detail: Doctrine provides a range of 1.25-1.40x for carriage-style doors. The low end (1.25x) applies to simple crossbuck overlays. The high end (1.40x) applies to elaborate decorative hardware + overlay + window combinations. A single modifier value may not capture this range well.
uncertainties.recommendation: Use 1.30x as the default carriage modifier. Allow override for elaborate carriage designs. Window modifier (+0.5-1.5 hrs) is additive and separate from the carriage panel modifier.

uncertainties.detail: Doctrine does not provide a precise scaling factor for double vs single doors. Estimate of 1.80-2.00x is inferred: double doors have ~2x the SF but share setup/cleanup fixed costs with single doors. The actual ratio depends on how much of the total time is fixed (setup/cleanup) vs variable (application).
uncertainties.recommendation: Use 1.85x as default double-door modifier. Field calibration recommended.

uncertainties.detail: Wax removal is described qualitatively (gray 3M pad + cleaner) but no precise time-per-SF rate is given in doctrine. Estimated at 0.50-1.0 hrs/EA for a single door based on the cleaning protocol complexity.
uncertainties.recommendation: Include wax removal in the base prep rate for steel doors. Flag for field calibration.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Mandatory full cover for spray. Canvas drops minimum for brush/roll.
zones.notes: Driveway directly below garage door. High overspray risk during spray. Canvas drops or absorbent mats (NOT standard poly — slippery safety hazard). Broom-finish concrete is porous and hard to clean.
Siding panels adjacent to garage door opening. Pre-taped poly or masking film. Overspray risk when spraying garage door face. No separate PS key — included in per-door setup estimate.
Window inserts in garage door panels. HDPE static-cling film for each pane. Carriage-style divided lites require individual masking. Time driven by window count as additive modifier (+0.5-1.5 hrs).
Weatherstripping contact surfaces along sides and top of door. Mask to prevent paint contamination. Paint destroys seal flexibility.
Track and roller contact points, spring mechanism hardware. Must NOT be painted — causes binding. Mask before spray application.
Bottom weatherseal (astragal). Either remove before painting or mask. Prop door 2-4 inches during cure. Dedicated management task.

protection_zones_analysis.cross_spec_protection_note: Garage door trim/casing protection during siding spray is NOT this spec's responsibility — belongs to siding or trim spec. Driveway protection IS this spec's responsibility.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Garage door casing/trim surrounds the door opening. Different color/sheen from garage door face. Casing is painted by SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1. Masking required when spraying door.
Siding terminates at garage door casing. No direct adjacency between garage door face and siding — casing intervenes. Masking of siding required during spray.
Driveway/apron directly below garage door bottom edge. Protection target — not painted. Full cover required during spray operations.
Garage interior ceiling above door opening (header area). May receive overspray when door is open during painting. Light masking if door is painted while open.

adjacency_analysis.key_finding: Garage door has minimal edge work because it is a self-contained panel assembly. All adjacencies are protection targets, not cut-in lines. The casing belongs to the trim spec.

affected_conditions.notes: Garage doors are always at ground level. No height modifier. The door itself provides the full work surface at ground level (opened manually or with opener for leapfrog technique).

excluded_conditions.rationale: Environmental conditions are unpredictable at bid time. They are SOP/process concerns, not estimatable. Per sibling exterior spec pattern.

excluded.reason: Affects spray drift management. Halt spray above 10 mph. Not estimatable.
Steel doors absorb significant heat in direct sun. Schedule for cooler hours. Not estimatable at bid time.
Weather-dependent. Not predictable at bid time.
Affects LRV restriction enforcement and drying but not production rate estimation.

valid_input_states.rationale: NC garage doors arrive in one of these three states. Steel doors are factory-primed (dominant — ~85%). Wood doors are bare. Bare metal is rare in NC (occurs when factory primer is damaged). SS_EXT_PRIMED_FIELD is excluded because garage doors are not field-primed as a separate mobilization in NC — they arrive from the factory and are painted in one pass.
valid_input_states.notes: Unlike entry doors, factory-primed steel garage doors STILL need DTM primer because the wax contamination makes factory primer unreliable.

output_state.rationale: Output state is the painted finish. Semi-gloss is the most common garage door sheen. Actual output varies by project sheen selection.

adjacent_state_protection_analysis.rationale: Protect finished casing from garage door spray overspray. Even unfinished casing gets light masking to keep it clean for subsequent trim painting.
Siding near garage door opening gets overspray during garage door painting. Full mask if finished, light mask if unfinished.
Driveway always needs full cover protection regardless of state. Porous concrete absorbs paint permanently.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Factory-applied polyester or fluorocarbon (Kynar) finish on steel garage door. Includes residual wax layer from fabrication/transit.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Wax removal (gray 3M pad + biodegradable cleaner) + degloss (120-150 grit or liquid deglosser) + ASTM D3359 adhesion verification.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: DTM acrylic primer. Factory primer alone is NOT adequate due to wax contamination.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Dominant NC state for steel garage doors (~85%). Unlike entry doors, factory-primed steel garage doors STILL require DTM primer because the wax removal protocol compromises the factory primer layer.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Raw uncoated wood garage door panels — no primer, no stain, no finish.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Sand to remove mill glaze (120-grit). Fill defects with exterior wood filler. Spot-prime knots on tannin-rich species.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: 100% acrylic latex exterior primer. Alkyd stain-blocker for cedar/redwood. Six-side sealing mandatory per DASMA TDS #162.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Wood panel garage doors. Six-side sealing includes back face, top/bottom edges, and all panel edges.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Raw ferrous metal garage door — no factory primer. Rare in NC (occurs when factory primer is damaged).
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Solvent clean + TSP wash. Active rust: SSPC-SP3 (power tool) or SSPC-SP7 (brush-off blast). Dents: body filler + finish-sand.
exterior_substrate_states.primer_type: Zinc-rich epoxy or DTM alkyd primer for carbon steel.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Rare in NC. Most steel doors arrive factory-primed. This state occurs when factory primer is severely damaged during transit/installation.

single_flush_steel_spray_total.notes: Total all-in rate for single flush steel door (56-63 SF). Includes: setup/masking, wax removal, degloss, DTM prime, 2 finish coats (leapfrog technique), bottom seal management, cleanup. QT3 baseline.

double_flush_steel_spray_total.notes: Total all-in rate for double flush steel door (112-126 SF). ~1.85x single door. QT3 baseline.

wax_removal_degloss_single.notes: Wax removal (3M pad + cleaner) + degloss (120-150 grit) + ASTM D3359 test. Single door.

wax_removal_degloss_double.notes: Wax removal + degloss for double door.

prime_coat_spray_single.notes: DTM primer spray application, single door (56-63 SF at 150-300 SF/hr spray rate).

finish_coat_spray_single.notes: Per finish coat, spray application, single door. Leapfrog technique adds ~15% over continuous spray. 2 coats needed.

masking_setup_spray_single.notes: Driveway protection + adjacent siding masking + weatherstrip masking + track/hardware masking. Single door, spray method.

masking_setup_spray_double.notes: Masking setup for double door. Wider driveway protection zone.

bottom_seal_management.notes: Remove bottom seal or prop door during cure. Per door regardless of size.

window_masking.notes: Per door when windows present. Depends on lite count. Simple insert = 0.50 hrs. Divided-lite carriage = 1.0-1.5 hrs.

six_side_seal_wood.notes: Additional time for wood door six-side sealing (back face, all edges). Single door. Brush work for edges.

cleanup_teardown_single.notes: Remove masking, clean tools, site cleanup. Single door.

sand_between_coats_qt4.notes: Light sand between finish coats with 220-grit. QT4 only. Single door.

spray_production_rates_sf.spray_application: 150-300 SF/hr (garage door panels — large flat surfaces ideal for spray)
spray_production_rates_sf.roller_application: 100-150 SF/hr (wood panel doors where roller is acceptable)

key_decisions.decision: This spec uses EA (each door) as the primary UOM via PS_EXT_OPENING_EA.DOOR_GARAGE.
key_decisions.rationale: Garage doors are discrete assemblies. Size (single/double) and complexity (flush/raised/carriage/windows) are modifiers within EA. The PS key counts doors without distinguishing size.

key_decisions.decision: Combined (full phase_scope). Prime and finish phases have unique task keys within the single spec.
key_decisions.rationale: NC garage doors are a single-mobilization scope — same crew primes and paints. Matches sibling exterior spec pattern.

key_decisions.decision: door_substrate (steel/wood/carriage) is a CONFIGURATION DIMENSION — changes task structure, primer system, and prep protocol.
key_decisions.rationale: Each substrate has fundamentally different prep workflow: steel = wax removal + degloss + DTM. Wood = sand + six-side seal + tannin management. Carriage = mixed-material prep + overlay detail. These are workflow branches, not simple rate modifiers.

key_decisions.decision: panel_complexity (flush/raised_panel/carriage/windows) is a MODIFIER DIMENSION — changes rate but not task structure (except windows adds masking tasks).
key_decisions.rationale: Flush, raised_panel, and carriage all follow the same task sequence but at different speeds. Windows adds a masking task. Modifiers: flush 1.00x, raised_panel 1.10x, carriage 1.25-1.40x, windows +0.5-1.5 hrs.

key_decisions.decision: Quality tier range is QT3-QT4. QT2 excluded (visible from street). QT5 excluded (utility surface).
key_decisions.rationale: Garage doors are visible from the street (not economy-appropriate) but are utility surfaces (not fine-finish appropriate). Two-tier range matches the practical quality spectrum for garage doors. Entry doors (SF_DOOR_EXT_NC_v1) support QT5 because they are architectural focal points.

key_decisions.topic: Factory-primed steel still needs DTM primer
key_decisions.decision: Factory-primed steel garage doors require DTM primer over the factory finish AFTER wax removal and deglossing.
key_decisions.rationale: Different from exterior entry doors where factory primer is adequate. Garage door factory finish has wax contamination that compromises the factory primer layer. DTM provides a fresh adhesion bridge after the wax removal protocol disturbs the factory coating.

key_decisions.topic: Application method — spray primary, no back-roll on steel
key_decisions.decision: Spray is the primary method. No back-rolling on steel (introduces orange peel). Brush for detail work on raised panels and carriage elements. Roller acceptable on wood panels only.
key_decisions.rationale: Per Application Methods Doctrine: metal doors should be spray-only. Large flat panels of garage doors are ideal for spray. Brush/roll secondary for detail work and wood substrate.

key_decisions.decision: Leapfrog painting technique is MANDATORY for all sectional garage doors — not a separate billable task but a process instruction that modifies execution of the spray/apply tasks.
key_decisions.rationale: Paint bridging across articulation joints is a critical failure mode. Leapfrog prevents this. The time impact (~15% overhead on apply tasks) is embedded in the production rate, not broken out as a separate task.

key_decisions.topic: Door size as modifier (not configuration dimension)
key_decisions.decision: Door size (single/double) is a MODIFIER DIMENSION, not a configuration dimension. Same task structure, different rates.
key_decisions.rationale: Single and double doors follow identical task sequences. Double doors simply have more SF to cover. Modifier: double = 1.85x of single.

key_decisions.decision: Only the street-facing exterior face is in scope. Garage-interior face is not scoped except for DASMA six-side sealing obligation on wood doors.
key_decisions.rationale: Standard NC practice for garage doors. Interior face is typically left as factory finish (steel) or may be a separate interior scope. Wood doors get back-face priming/sealing per DASMA TDS #162 but not full finish.

key_decisions.decision: Carriage/composite: HARD STOP at LRV < 55. Steel: LRV > 30 recommended, IR-reflective below 30. Wood: no hard LRV limit but dark colors stress substrate.
key_decisions.rationale: Per Exterior_Garage_Doors_Doctrine.md §4 and Exterior_Color_Sheen_Configuration_Doctrine.md §1. Thermal deformation risk varies by substrate material.

key_decisions.decision: EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers. Per sibling spec pattern.
key_decisions.rationale: Environmental conditions are unpredictable at bid time. SOP procedure notes, not production rate modifiers.

required_paintscope_keys.description: Count of garage doors in scope (single or double, any width)
TRUE when surfaces are new construction
SF of driveway surface within overspray/drip zone during painting

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Substrate material drives primer system, prep protocol, and failure mode profile. Must be captured per door because a project can have mixed types (e.g., main garage is steel, side carriage house is wood). Cannot be derived from other keys.
proposed_new_keys.alternative: Could be a project-level default with per-door override.

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Door size is the primary SF driver for production rate scaling within the EA-based counting system. Single = 56-63 SF, double = 112-126 SF. Must be captured per door.
proposed_new_keys.alternative: Could derive from physical dimensions if PaintScope captures door width.

proposed_new_keys.rationale: Panel complexity is the secondary production rate driver. Flush = 1.00x, raised = 1.10x, carriage = 1.25-1.40x. Windows is additive (+0.5-1.5 hrs). Captured per door during scope walkthrough.
proposed_new_keys.alternative: Windows could be a separate boolean flag rather than a panel_type value, since windows can coexist with any panel type.
